newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Acer out, others on outlook.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Acer out, others on outlook.

text.p: Asian debt markets offered a couple of new issues on Thursday and news of more to come.
Acer Holdings International, a wholly owned subsidiary of Singapore-listed Acer Computer International, launched a US$50 million floating rate note.

The five-year issue has puts and calls in years three and four. It pays a margin of 50 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 57 basis points to top tier managers.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and IBJ Asia are lead managers.

The issue includes an ownership covenant requiring Taiwan-listed Acer Inc to maintain a 51 percent stake in Acer Computer International until August 1998 and a share of more than 41 percent thereafter for the life of the issue.
In London, Korea Development Bank set a 70 billion yen bond through lead manager Nomura International. The 1.875 percent five-year bond was priced at par.
Bankers said Bank Negara Indonesia could launch its 10-year US$145 million Yankee bond during New York hours today. The notes were rated BBB by Standard and Poor's Corp earlier today.
J.P. Morgan reportedly is the lead manager of BNI's issue.
Response to the issue already has been positive, Asian bankers said. They said the upcoming and long-awaited bond for State Development Bank of China also is looking good.
While Asian markets have featured a few blockbuster Yankee or Eurobond deals so far this year, the more local floating rate note market has been relatively quiet.
Borrowers are still weighing their options, bankers said.

They said the top-tier South Korean commercial banks continue to command tight pricing, despite the country's recent turmoil sparked by a controversial labour law and a dwindling number of lending banks willing or able to hold low yielding Korean bank paper on their books.

"We tried to get the mandate for one issue but another bank was offering an all-in of five basis points less than the borrower's last issue and that was 2.5 basis points narrower than we wanted to go," said a syndicate manager at a European bank, who declined to name the borrower.
The mystery borrower could be A2-rated Shinhan Bank, which reportedly has been offered all-in pricing of less than 20 basis points over LIBOR for three-year paper.
Among the other possibilites are Cho Hung Bank and Korea Long-Term Credit Bank, which bankers said also are taking bids. Mandates are expected very soon.
As was the case last year, bankers expect European banks to be the big takers of Korean issues.
Japanese banks, which historically have been big lenders to Korea, cut back last year as yields declined and are now looking at issues that offer better returns.
"They are looking at higher spreads, but the problem is that head offices are worried about taking on risk," said a banker with a Japanese client base.
"Some banks are looking at taking longer-maturity bonds and swapping them back to floating rate," he added.
In other news, Hongkong Bank increased its five-year floating rate certificate of deposit issue to HK$3.5 billion from HK$2.0 billion.
It also boosted the size of its CD issuance programme to HK$20 billion from HK$15 billion to accomodate the increased issue.
